item.title: Vespers: Addiction & Recovery Service — Sun Sep 20, 5:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Addiction & Recovery Service Sunday, September 20 | 5:00 PM
In the Sanctuary On Sunday, September 20, we will hold our annual Addiction and Recovery Service as part of Recovery Month at our 5:00 PM Vespers gathering. This service is open to anyone whose life has been touched by addiction — those in recovery, those still struggling and the family members, friends and loved ones who walk alongside them. Addiction carries a particular kind of pain — one that is often carried in silence, and one that ripples outward to touch everyone who loves the person affected. In this service, we hold that pain honestly and without judgment, naming it before God as a community that refuses to look away. And in the same breath, we give thanks for the healing and hope that recovery makes possible: the daily courage it takes, the grace that sustains it, and the deep truth that no one walks this road alone. item.title: Evening Compline — Sun Sep 20, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Sep 23, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.

item.description: Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 Presented by Scott Weidensaul, author of “The Return of the Oystercatcher: Saving Birds to Save the Planet” At a time when the news for birds – for the planet – has rarely seemed more grim, there is reason for hope. We’ve restored faltering bird populations in the past, bringing back once nearly extinct raptors and waterfowl. And despite the odds today, all around the world, people are actually reviving bird populations, providing a roadmap for wider recovery. item.title: "where time folds:" A Community Conversation — Sat Oct 17, 1:00 PM — The Stevens & Smith Center
item.description:
“where time folds:” A Community Conversation
In celebration of National Black Poets Day, Lancaster’s Inaugural Poet Laureate Evita Colón invites the community to engage with “where time folds,” the original poem she wrote for the grand opening of the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center. Co-presented by LancasterHistory, this gathering explores the role of Black poets as storytellers, historians, interpreters, and witnesses—and the ways poetry can help us understand the places we call home.
Through a close reading of selected stanzas, attendees will unpack the poem’s metaphors, imagery, and layered storytelling, inviting participants to consider what lies beneath the language. Together, we’ll explore how Black poetry has carried history, challenged dominant narratives, preserved memory, and imagined possibility.

item.description: Carl Groff will lead this easy walking field trip west along the trail with a stop at the Hershey Trust Wetlands overlook, and then continue west with views of open fields, woodland, and creeks. item.title: Monthly Club Meeting - “In Search of 10,000, and 10,000, and 10,000 Birds” — Thu Nov 12, 7:00 PM — North Museum of Nature and Science
item.description: Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 Presented by Peter Kaestner, legendary birder and retired diplomat Peter Kaestner relates his life-long quest to see 10,000 species of birds – a quest that was almost derailed on February, 2024, when another birder claimed the record just hours before Peter saw is last bird in the Philippines. Since then, Peter has maintained his quest, ultimately observing 10,000 species in the eBird and AviList taxonomies. Peter is a retired U.S. diplomat and an active independent birder who has spent a lifetime sharing his passion. On February 9, 2024, he achieved his ultimate goal when he saw his 10,000th species of bird, an Orange-tufted Spiderhunter in Mindanao, the Philippines on the IOC taxonomy. On October 21, 2025, he reached 10,000 on eBird, and on November 11, 2025, he recorded his 10,000th species on the new AviList harmonized world bird list. item.description:

item.title: Monthly Club Meeting - "Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies" — Thu Dec 10, 7:00 PM — North Museum of Nature and Science
item.description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 Presented by Club President Andy McGann Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.
Source: Lancaster Bird Club

item.title: Wednesday Morning's Breakfast Rides Casual Pace Variable Distance RSVP Required — Wed Sep 16, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup It's September and time to change our breakfast rides to 9am... Every Wednesday morning...Ride and eat Yummy breakfast together.
Please do not go on this ride unless you will ride at a casual pace and stay with the group . We will meet to ride to breakfast at a casual pace. After eating some may split up with some returning to the start and others going longer and faster.
Helmets are mandatory; No ear buds or audible music playing devices. Please bring water, and a basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump/CO2 inflator).
To eliminate passing around a pen and paper waiver, we encourage LBC Club membership and Meetup RSVP below to join this ride. RSVP also allows us to contact you after the ride if needed. If you do not RSVP you are not covered by the club excess accident insurance policy; only club members who RSVP are covered. Being on Meetup does not mean you are a club member. Join here- https://www.lancasterbikeclub.net/content.aspx?page_

item.description:
Loss of a Spouse GriefShare is for women and men who have lost their spouses. While all loss is significant, a spouse’s loss can come with its own unique hardship and pain. If you are still reeling from your spouse’s departure from life, this group is for you. Loss of a Spouse meets for 13 weeks in the fall and spring on Wednesday afternoons from 3:00-4:30pm. Register https://www.griefshare.org/groups/264485
Source: Calvary Church
